consent.instrument: Synthetic sample; no human-subject consent instrument.
consent.scope: Bundled de-identified synthetic lesson-study discourse for local SENA pilot verification.

retention.policy: Retain generated synthetic sample artifacts only for local verification and reproducibility review.

interactions.evidence: Ms Lee asks Mr Chan to connect the learning goal to prior evidence；李老師請陳老師把學習目標連到證據
Mr Chan invites Dr Wong to check whether the task supports explanation
Dr Wong replies with a critique of the opening prompt
Ms Ho notes how Ms Lee responds to student evidence
Ms Lee asks Ms Ho to watch for explanation quality
Mr Chan builds on Ms Ho's observation during reflection
Ms Ho asks Dr Wong to help interpret the evidence pattern；何老師請黃博士協助解讀證據模式
Dr Wong links the critique back to the revised design

utterances.text: We need a question that makes students explain the pattern instead of only naming it
The worksheet can ask learners to compare two examples before they write a hypothesis
That is promising but the prompt needs a place for evidence and a place for explanation
Several students gave evidence but only one group explained why the pattern held；學生用圖形做證據但還未說清楚原因
I observed that the group with stronger coordination challenged each other before agreeing
So the next prompt should ask them to critique the first explanation before finalizing it
The evidence suggests the design improved participation but the explanation link is still uneven
I think the observer notes show when coordination became a bridge to reasoning；觀課紀錄顯示協作慢慢變成推理的橋
Our revision should keep the evidence comparison and add a reflection checkpoint
Then the next cycle can test whether critique strengthens the evidence explanation pair

codebook.label: Evidence
codebook.description: Observation or data used to support a claim

codebook.label: Explanation

codebook.description: Review of learning design progress or quality
